memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people. They responded, 'We will do everything the Lord has said; we will obey.'" - Exodus 24:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The covenant is read aloud, and the people respond again: "We will do everything the Lord has said; we will obey." This time they add that word — obey, which carries the sense of listening attentively and then acting. It is not enough to hear God's word; it must be lived. They commit to both.

Notice that God read them the terms before asking for their agreement. He did not trick them or hide the cost. He laid out His words plainly, and they responded with open eyes. There is honesty in how God deals with His people. He tells us the truth about what following Him involves, and then invites our wholehearted response.

James picks up this very theme, urging us not to merely listen to the word but to do what it says, or we deceive ourselves (Jas 1:22). It is possible to hear sermons, read Scripture, and nod along without our lives changing at all. Real hearing shows up in real living. Yet we know from Israel's story that good intentions are not enough — we need God's Spirit to empower what our hearts sincerely intend. Ask Him today not just to help you hear His Word, but to work it deeply into how you actually live.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I a hearer of God's Word only, or does it genuinely shape how I live?
What has God clearly said that I have been slow to actually obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from merely hearing Your Word without living it. By Your Spirit, work Your truth so deeply into me that it changes how I actually live each day. Amen.
